                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 When they <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> at the great stone which <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> in Gibeon, Amasa went before them <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Having gathered some Forces, and given due Orders for the rest to follow him, he returned to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> and by the Kings Command went after those mentioned <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 7. and being come up to them at the place where they waited for him, he put himself into the Head of <ns0:hi>Ioab</ns0:hi>'s men, and the <ns0:hi>Cher<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>thites</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Pelethites,</ns0:hi> and such as he had brought along with him, and Marched before them as their Chief and General.</ns0:note>; and Jo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />abs garment that he had put on, was girded unto him <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">After the manner of Travellers and Soldiers.</ns0:note>, and upon it a <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb</ns0:hi> Girdle; or, belt of a Sword.</ns0:note> girdle <ns0:hi>with</ns0:hi> a sword fast<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned upon his loins in the sheath thereof, and as he went forth <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">To meet and Salute <ns0:hi>Amasa,</ns0:hi> who was coming towards him to do him Honor.</ns0:note> it fell out <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Things having (it is likely) been so contrived by <ns0:hi>Ioab,</ns0:hi> that upon the least Moti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on of his Body, his Sword should drop out, and he might take it up without raising <ns0:hi>Amasa</ns0:hi>'s Suspition.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 And Joab said to Amasa, <ns0:hi>Art</ns0:hi> thou in health, my brother? And Joab took Amasa by the beard <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">As the manner of Ancient times was, when they kissed and saluted one another.</ns0:note> with the right hand to kiss him.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 But Amasa took no heed to the sword that <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> in Joabs hand <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Which falling out, as it seemed, casually, he supposed that <ns0:hi>Ioab</ns0:hi> intended onely to put it into its Scabbard, and therefore took no care to defend himself against the stroke.</ns0:note>: so he smote him therewith in the fifth <ns0:hi>rib</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">See on <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 2. 23.</ns0:note>, and shed out his bowels to the ground, and <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> doubled not his <ns0:hi>stroke.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> strook him not again <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">He dispatched him at one stroke; or, gave him his Deaths Wound at the first blow, and need<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed not to smite him again.</ns0:note>, and he died: so Joab <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Who now boldly resumed his former Place, and Marched in the Head of the Army. It is not strange, that <ns0:hi>Amasa</ns0:hi>'s Soldiers did not fight to Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venge his Death; partly, because not many of them were yet come up, but came by degrees, as the following Verses <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>hew; and partly, because <ns0:hi>Ioab</ns0:hi>'s Interest and Authority with the Military-men was very great; especially, with <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s Guards, who were here present, and who had no kindness for <ns0:hi>Amasa,</ns0:hi> as having been the General of the Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bellious Army; and, as they might think, was not fit to be put into a Place of so great Power and Trust.</ns0:note> and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 And one of Joabs men <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Left there on purpose to deliver the following Message.</ns0:note> stood by him, and said, He that favoureth Joab <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">He that would have <ns0:hi>Ioab</ns0:hi> to be General, rather than such a Perfideous Rebel and Traytor as <ns0:hi>Amasa<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                        </ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>, and he that <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> for David <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">He that wisheth <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> good success against <ns0:hi>Sheba,</ns0:hi> and against all Rebels. Whereby he implies, that though this Fact of his was done against the Kings Command, yet it was for his Interest and Defence.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>let him go</ns0:hi> after Joab.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:266" />12 And Amasa wallowed <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>rolled himself,</ns0:hi> being in the Pangs of Death; yet having so much Life left, as to move himself a little, though not to raise himself up from his place.</ns0:note> in blood <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">In his own blood, which was shed there.</ns0:note> in the midst of the high-way: and when the man saw that all the people <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">To wit, the Soldiers which were upon their March.</ns0:note> stood still <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Wondering at the Spectacle, and enquiring into the Author and occasion of it.</ns0:note>, he removed Amasa out of the high-way into the field <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Perceiving, that it both incensed them against <ns0:hi>Ioab,</ns0:hi> and hindred the Kings present Service.</ns0:note>, and cast a cloth upon him, when he saw that every one that came by him, stood still.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 When he was removed out of the high<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />way, all the people went on after Joab, to pur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sue after Sheba the son of Bichri.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">¶ 14 And he <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Either, 1. <ns0:hi>Ioab,</ns0:hi> who pursued <ns0:hi>Sheba</ns0:hi> through all the Tribes as far as <ns0:hi>Abel.</ns0:hi> Or rather, 2. <ns0:hi>Sheba,</ns0:hi> who was last mentioned, who Marched from Tribe to Tribe to stir them up to Sedition; and to him the following words seem best to agree.</ns0:note> went through all the tribes of Israel unto Abel, and to Beth-maachah <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Or rather, <ns0:hi>to Abel, even to Bethmaachah; i. e.</ns0:hi> unto <ns0:hi>Abel-beth-maachah,</ns0:hi> as this place is called here in the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> text, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 15. and 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 15. 20. 2 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 15. 29. to distinguish it from other <ns0:hi>Abels;</ns0:hi> and to signifie, that this was that <ns0:hi>Abel</ns0:hi> which was in the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Nap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thali</ns0:hi> in the Northern border of <ns0:hi>Canaan</ns0:hi> towards that part of <ns0:hi>Syria</ns0:hi> called <ns0:hi>Maachah,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 10. 8.</ns0:note>, and all the Berites <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Such as lived in the City, or Territory of <ns0:hi>Beeroth</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Benjamin, Iosh.</ns0:hi> 18. 25. who being of the same Tribe, if not City with <ns0:hi>Sheba,</ns0:hi> and his greatest Acquaintance and Friends: or, being most Implacable against <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> adhered to <ns0:hi>Sheba,</ns0:hi> and followed him through all the Tribes of <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>: and they <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">to wit, the Tribes of <ns0:hi>Israel; i. e.</ns0:hi> a considerable Number of them; as might well be expected, when the discontents were so high and general.</ns0:note> were gathered toge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, and went also after him <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> After <ns0:hi>Sheba.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 And they <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e. Ioab</ns0:hi> and his Army, which is easily understood, both from the foregoing and following Verses.</ns0:note> came and besieged him in Abel of Bethmaachah, and they cast up a bank against the city <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">From whence they might either batter the Wall, or shoot at those who defended it against them, who should Assault it. See 2 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 19. 32. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 32. 24. and 33. 4. Otherwise, <ns0:hi>they threw down the bank of the City,</ns0:hi> which they had raised up to Defend the City on the weakest side.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> it stood against the outmost Wall.</ns0:note> it stood in the trench <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> The Bank stood in, or near to the Trench, or the Wall of the City; so that the City was in great danger of being taken. Otherwise, the City stood within the Trench, or Wall, being Defended onely by a single Trench, or a weak Wall; the Bank which was raised up there to Defend it, being thrown down.</ns0:note>: and all the people that <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> with Joab, † battered the wall to throw <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> down:<ns0:note place="margin">‡ <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> marred to throw down.</ns0:note>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 ¶ Then cried a wise woman out of the city, Hear, Hear; say, I pray you, unto Joab, Come near hither, that I may speak with thee.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17 And when he was come near unto her, the woman said, <ns0:hi>Art</ns0:hi> thou Joab? And he an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swered, <ns0:hi>I am he:</ns0:hi> Then she said unto him, Hear the words of thine handmaid. And he answered, I do hear.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 Then she spake, saying, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> They plainly speak in the begin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning, saying, Surely they will ask of <ns0:hi>A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bel,</ns0:hi> and so make an end.</ns0:note> They were wont to speak in old time, saying, They shall surely ask <ns0:hi>counsel</ns0:hi> at Abel: and so they ended <ns0:hi>the matters.</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:note place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>s</ns0:hi> According to this Translation the sence is, This City which thou art about to Destroy, is no mean and contemp<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tible one, but so honourable and considerable for its Wis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom, and the Wise People in it, that when any differences did arise among any of the Neighbours, they used Prover<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bially to say, <ns0:hi>We will ask the Opinion and Advice of the Men of</ns0:hi> Abel <ns0:hi>about it, and we will stand to their Arbitra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion; and so all parties were satisfied, and Disputes ended.</ns0:hi> But there is another Translation in the Margent, embraced also by some others, which seems to be the best; <ns0:hi>They (i. e.</ns0:hi> The Citizens of this City) <ns0:hi>plainly</ns0:hi> (or, <ns0:hi>commonly) spake</ns0:hi> (among themselves) <ns0:hi>in the beginning</ns0:hi> (to wit, when <ns0:hi>Sheba</ns0:hi> and his Men first came into the City, and they were infor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />med, That <ns0:hi>Ioab</ns0:hi> was pursuing him) <ns0:hi>saying, Surely they will ask of Abel, and so make an end: i. e.</ns0:hi> They will peace<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ably Expostulate the business with us, and enquire, Why we received <ns0:hi>Sheba</ns0:hi> into our City? and whether we would de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />liver him up into their hands, and would inform us of the reason of their Hostile Attempt upon us, and offer to us Conditions of Peace, which by Gods Law <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 20. 10. they were to do even to strange, and much more to <ns0:hi>Israeli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tish</ns0:hi> Cities. So she doth both modestly reprove <ns0:hi>Ioab</ns0:hi> for the neglect of his Duty, and oblige him to the Performance of it.</ns0:note>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 I <ns0:hi>am one of them that are</ns0:hi> peaceable <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> faithful in Israel <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>I</ns0:hi> (to wit, the City of <ns0:hi>Abel,</ns0:hi> in whose Name and Person she speaks this) am one of the <ns0:hi>peaceable and faith<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful</ns0:hi> Cities <ns0:hi>of Israel.</ns0:hi> Whatsoever <ns0:hi>Sheba</ns0:hi> may design, whom we have innocently received into our City, before we well understood the matter; We of this City abhor the thoughts of Warring, and Rebelling against the King, as having had no hand in <ns0:hi>Absalom</ns0:hi>'s late Rebellion: which is probable enough, considering both their Scituation in the utmost Bor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ders of the Land, very remote from the Seat of that Civil War; and their open Profession of their Peaceableness, and Fidelity, or Loyalty to the King; which had been Impu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dent if they had been so lately Involved in the last War and Rebellion.</ns0:note>: thou seekest to destroy a city, and a mother <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i e.</ns0:hi> A Mother City: for great Cities are com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />monly called <ns0:hi>Mothers;</ns0:hi> as lesser Towns or Villages subject to them, and depending upon them, for Direction and De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fence, are called their <ns0:hi>Daughters,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 16. 27, 46.</ns0:note> in Israel: why wilt thou swallow up the inheritance of the LORD <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> A considerable part of that Land which God hath chosen for his peculiar Possession. The Destruction which thou art about to bring upon us, is an injury also to <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> and to the God of <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20 And Joab answered and said, Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up, or destroy.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">21 The matter <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> not so: but a man of mount Ephraim <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>Qu.</ns0:hi> How can this be so, when he is called a <ns0:hi>Benjamite? ver.</ns0:hi> 1. <ns0:hi>Answ.</ns0:hi> Either he was a <ns0:hi>Benjamite</ns0:hi> by Birth, but dwelt in the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Ephraim,</ns0:hi> as many did upon several occasions dwell out of their own Tribes: or, <ns0:hi>mount Ephraim</ns0:hi> was a place in <ns0:hi>Benjamin,</ns0:hi> which might be so called, either because it was upon the Borders of <ns0:hi>Ephraim,</ns0:hi> and looked to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wards it; or from some notable Action or Event of the <ns0:hi>Ephraimites</ns0:hi> in that place. Comp. <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 18. 6.</ns0:note> (Sheba the son of Bichri <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> by <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> Name.</ns0:note> by name) hath lift up his hand <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Ta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken up Arms, or raised Rebellion.</ns0:note> against the king, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> against David: deliver him onely, and I will de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />part from the city. And the woman said unto Joab, Behold, his head shall be thrown to thee over the wall <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Which she undertook, because she knew the present temper, and great fears of the Citizens, and Soldiers too; and that considering their evi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dent and extream Danger, they were generally desirous of Peace, from which they were restrained onely by <ns0:hi>Sheba</ns0:hi>'s Authority and Interest; and therefore did not doubt by God's Blessing upon her Wise Counsel to effect it, as in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deed she did. And it is not unlikely, that this Woman might be a Governess in that City. For though this Office was commonly performed by Men; yet were not the Wo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />men wholly Excluded, but sometimes Imployed in the Go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vernment: As we see in <ns0:hi>Deborah,</ns0:hi> who Judged <ns0:hi>Israel, Iudg.</ns0:hi> 4. 4. And Queen <ns0:hi>Athalia,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 11.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="22">22 Then the woman went unto all the people in her wisdom <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Prudently Treated with them about it, either severally or joyntly, as she saw fit; representing to them the cer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tainty and nearness of all their Ruine, if they did not spee<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dily comply with her Desires, and certain Deliverance if they did.</ns0:note>, and they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and cast <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> out to Joab: and he blew a trumpet, and they <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>Ioab</ns0:hi> and his Army which Besieged them.</ns0:note> † retired from<ns0:note place="margin">‡ <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> scattered.</ns0:note> the city, every man to his tent: and Joab retur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned to Jerusalem unto the king.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="23">23 ¶ Now <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>

                     </ns0:note> Joab <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> over all the host of Is<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rael <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">The good success of this, and of former Expedi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, under the conduct of <ns0:hi>Ioab,</ns0:hi> had so fixed his Interest in the Army, and others of <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s fastest Friends, that the King could not, without danger to the publick weal displace him.</ns0:note>: and Benajah the son of Jehoiadah <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> over the Cherethites, and over the Pelethites.</ns0:p>

                  <ns0:p n="25">25 And Sheba <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> scribe, and Zadok and Abi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />athar <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> the priests <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">See 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 8. 17. and 15. 35.</ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="26">26 And Ira also the Jairite <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">So called from his birth or dwelling in the Countrey of <ns0:hi>Iair</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Gilead, Numb.</ns0:hi> 32. 41. <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 10. 4.</ns0:note> was <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
